rounds.text: Jayant Infratech Ltd is trading at a compelling discount, marked by a modest P/E of 12x [E1] and an even more attractive 5.67x against a sector benchmark of 13.66x [E6]. The business demonstrates impressive historical growth, featuring a 5-year compounded sales growth of 26% [E14] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% [E17]. Profitability metrics are robust, with an ROE of 15.41% [E9] and a 5-year median return on equity of 16% [E22], outperforming the sector benchmark ROE of 10.57% [E9]. Operational efficiency is clearly expanding as evidenced by a yearly operating-margin trend that has been increasing over the last four years [E27], highlighted by a quarterly operating margin reaching 17% in September 2026 compared to 8% in the year-ago quarter [E26]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 394 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 69.8% [E38], while the reverse DCF implies the current market price only requires a modest 1.4% earnings growth [E39]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased by 15.59 percentage points over the last three years to 55.85% [E35], and operating cash flow dropped to negative Rs 13 Cr in March 2026 [E30].

Despite reported bottom-line profits, the business suffers from a severe cash generation crisis, highlighted by a negative cash conversion of -1.62x and an operating cash flow of Rs -13 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30]. This cash drain extends to free cash flow, which plummeted to Rs -14 Cr over the same period, while total borrowings simultaneously escalated to Rs 40 Cr by Sep 2026 [E31, E33]. Top-line expansion is stalling, demonstrated by a contraction in compounded sales growth to -7% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. Furthermore, insider commitment is waning as promoters have actively reduced their stake by 15.59 percentage points down to 55.85% over the past three years [E35, E45]. Compounded share price growth over a three-year span sits in negative territory at -3%, accompanied by a complete absence of shareholder returns via a 0.00% dividend yield [E20, E4, E44]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 12 and maintains a strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% [E1, E17].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -13 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -14 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31], alongside a zero dividend yield [E4, E44]. However, the cash drain must be viewed against stellar profitability and margin expansion, evidenced by a rising operating margin reaching 17% in Sep 2026 compared to 8% in the year-ago quarter [E26], and an overall increasing trend over the last 4 years [E27]. While borrowings rose to Rs 40 Cr [E33], leverage remains moderate at 0.61x [E32], while core profitability metrics easily outpace sector benchmarks, including an ROA of 9.09% versus 4.7% [E8] and an ROE of 15.41% versus 10.57% [E9]. The purported top-line stall over the trailing twelve months [E16] ignores strong historical compounding of 26% over 5 years and 38% over 3 years [E14, E15], backed by recent quarterly results showing net profit up 100% YoY [E48]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased over 3 years [E35, E45], yet insiders still retain a majority control of 55.85% [E35], and the depressed share price growth of -3% over 3 years [E20] has already reversed with a 52% gain over the past year [E21] while trading at a cheap P/E of 5.67x against sector benchmarks [E6].

Conceded: operating margins reached 17% in Sep 2026 [E26] and historical 5-year sales compounded at 26% [E14]. However, citing these historical figures ignores the severe top-line contraction of -7% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. The bull points to a P/E of 5.67x [E6] and a 52% 1-year price gain [E21], but fails to address that 3-year share price growth sits at a negative -3% [E20] while price growth recently outpaces profit growth by 50% [E41]. Conceded: insiders still hold 55.85% [E35]. Nevertheless, this represents a significant and ongoing promoter dilution of 15.59 percentage points since Sep 2022 [E35]. While the bull highlights moderate leverage of 0.61x [E32], borrowings actually expanded to Rs 40 Cr alongside a catastrophic cash drain of negative Rs 13 Cr in operating cash flow and negative Rs 14 Cr in free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E30, E31, E33]. Finally, stellar profit percentages ring hollow when cash conversion plunges to -1.62x and the company completely withholds dividends from shareholders [E4, E29, E44].
